_README: INSTITUTION TIERS - a configuration file, not code.
Maintainers edit THIS file to add or re-tier an institution. Nothing in
src/ hardcodes an institution name. GET /rubric/institutions serves this
file so an administrator can read the live classification without shell
access.
DEMO/RESEARCH values. The tiers below are a proposal for a student
project and carry no authority. They need faculty approval before any
real use - set approved_by / approved_on when that happens.
HOW A NAME IS MATCHED
1. The institution string is normalised (lowercased, punctuation
stripped, ampersand to 'and', whitespace collapsed).
2. Aliases are expanded - abbreviations, former names, merged names.
3. never_match is checked, so a lookalike cannot claim a tier.
4. Each tier's patterns are tried IN FILE ORDER; first match wins,
and tier_1 is tried before tier_2 before tier_3. A campus-specific
pattern must therefore sit ABOVE any family-wide catch-all.
5. No match gives tier 'unknown', which earns the UNKNOWN multiplier
AND is flagged for human review. It is never silently penalised.
WHY PATTERNS AND NOT A NAME LIST: CVs print 'IIT Bombay', 'Indian
Institute of Technology Bombay' and 'I.I.T. Bombay' for one place. A
pattern absorbs the variation; a literal list would miss two of three.
A PATTERN MAY SET needs_review: true. That means the tier follows the
approved rule but the identification is not certain, so a human is
asked to confirm it. It is used for the family-wide IIT/NIT catch-alls,
where we know the family but not the campus.
tier_basis: The top/mid split for IITs and NITs follows FOUNDING ERA, not an annual
ranking, so the list is stable and does not need re-approval whenever a
TIER 1 IITs: the seven first-generation institutes - Kharagpur, Bombay,
TIER 1 NITs: Tiruchirappalli, Karnataka (Surathkal), Warangal, Rourkela,
TIER 1 also keeps IISc and the established non-IIT/NIT peers that were
already tier 1 - IIIT, BITS Pilani, IISER, ISI, IIM, IIEST, TIFR - and
the listed international institutions, so that (for example) an MIT
doctorate does not score below a mid-tier NIT one.
TIER 2: every other IIT (the 2008-onward institutes, IIT (BHU) Varanasi
and IIT (ISM) Dhanbad included) and every other NIT.
TIER 3: other recognised degree-awarding institutions - central, state,
deemed and private universities, and recognised universities abroad that
An IIT or NIT whose campus is not named in tier 1 or tier 2 still lands
in tier 2 under the rule 'every other IIT/NIT', but is FLAGGED so a
human confirms it rather than the list silently deciding.

tier_1.label: First-generation IITs, top NITs, IISc and established peers
tier_1.rationale: The seven first-generation IITs, IISc, the top NITs, and the centrally funded technical and research institutes of comparable standing, plus their direct international equivalents. Standing rests on statute and founding era rather than on a ranking that moves each year.

patterns.match: birla institute of technology and science
patterns.label: BITS Pilani

patterns.match: indian institute of science education and research
patterns.label: IISER

patterns.match: indian institute of engineering science and technology
patterns.label: IIEST

tier_2.label: Other IITs and NITs
tier_2.rationale: Indian Institutes of Technology and National Institutes of Technology that are not first-generation or top-ranked under tier 1. Institutes of national importance by statute, so the qualification carries the same legal standing; the tier reflects founding era only. Campus-specific patterns come first; the family-wide catch-alls at the end apply the approved rule 'every other IIT/NIT' but ask a human to confirm, because a name without a campus cannot be placed with certainty.

patterns.match: (indian institute of technology|\biit\b).*\b(dhanbad|indian school of mines)\b
patterns.label: IIT (ISM) Dhanbad

patterns.match: motilal nehru national institute of technology
patterns.label: MNNIT Allahabad

patterns.match: sardar vallabhbhai national institute of technology
patterns.label: SVNIT Surat

patterns.match: maulana azad national institute of technology
patterns.label: MANIT Bhopal
an IIT with no campus named
patterns.review_why: recognised as an Indian Institute of Technology, but the CV does not name a campus this configuration lists. The approved rule places any IIT outside the first-generation seven in tier 2, so that is what was applied - a first-generation campus written in an unusual way would belong in tier 1 instead. Please confirm which campus it is

patterns.label: an NIT with no campus named
patterns.review_why: recognised as a National Institute of Technology, but the CV does not name a campus this configuration lists. The approved rule places any NIT outside the top five in tier 2, so that is what was applied - a top-five campus written in an unusual way would belong in tier 1 instead. Please confirm which campus it is

tier_3.label: Other recognised degree-awarding institutions
tier_3.rationale: Central, state, deemed and private universities, and recognised universities abroad that are not named in tier 1. The qualification is unquestioned; the institution is not one of the nationally designated technical institutes in tiers 1 and 2. Listed here EXPLICITLY by a maintainer; this tier is NOT the destination for a name the configuration does not recognise, which becomes 'unknown' and is flagged instead.

patterns.match: university of mumbai|university of calcutta|university of madras|university of hyderabad|university of pune|university of rajasthan
patterns.label: State university

aliases._README: Expanded BEFORE tier matching. The key is matched as a whole word on the normalised string and replaced by the value. Covers abbreviations, former names and mergers. An alias must expand to a string the tier patterns can match: a campus-level abbreviation therefore expands to the full name INCLUDING the campus, because the tier of an IIT or NIT now depends on which campus it is.
aliases.mnnit: motilal nehru national institute of technology
aliases.svnit: sardar vallabhbhai national institute of technology
aliases.manit: maulana azad national institute of technology
aliases.bengal engineering and science universit: indian institute of engineering science and technology

never_match._README: Names that LOOK like a tiered institution but are a different body. Checked FIRST; a hit bars the named tier or tiers for that string. This is the guard against crediting an unrelated college for a famous acronym. Both tier_1 and tier_2 are barred for the IIT/NIT lookalikes, because tier_2 now ends in a family-wide IIT/NIT catch-all and a lookalike must not reach it.
